fit_surface_principal_axes — 3D geometry op

• Data kinds: points → surface_poly

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.fit_surface_principal_axes(points, degree: 'int' = 2, *, isotropy_ratio: 'float' = 0.95) -> 'dict' (to call the implementation directly, import measure3d; measure3d.fit_surface_principal_axes(points, degree: 'int' = 2, *, isotropy_ratio: 'float' = 0.95) -> 'dict'; from the registry, ops3d.get("fit_surface_principal_axes"))

Usage

Rotate a slanted warped surface to PCA axes, then fit polynomial z'=f(x',y').

The two largest principal axes span the local x/y plane and the smallest is local z. Returns center, row-vector axes, monomial powers, coefficients, local and original-frame fitted_points, unit normal at the centroid, and gradient-normalised geometric rms. degree is the total polynomial degree. A cloud whose two largest variances differ by less than isotropy_ratio is rejected because its in-plane principal directions are not identifiable. For degree one the returned normal agrees with fit_plane3 up to sign.
